description: schedule is deliberately unset. The workflow cron in .github/workflows/renovate.yaml decides when Renovate runs; a schedule here would only be a second gate that has to agree with it.

assignees is the notification channel for updates that need a human. assignAutomerge defaults to false, so Renovate assigns only the PRs it will NOT automerge - majors, and anything whose automerge is switched off. Routine patch bumps stay silent because they are never assigned.

platformAutomerge is off because GitHub's own auto-merge only arms on a PR that cannot merge yet - it needs a branch protection rule or ruleset withholding the merge. This repository deliberately has neither, so asking for it would be a no-op. Renovate merges the PRs itself instead, on the run after CI goes green.

abandonments:recommended sets abandonmentThreshold to a year, which matters here because most of these applications are community projects with no official image and several of their predecessors died quietly. It opens no PRs - dependencyDashboardReportAbandonment defaults to true, so it only lists them on the Dependency Dashboard.

customManagers.description: Sidecar images nested under vpn.* and metrics.*. Indented four spaces or more so the top-level image block is left to the helm-values manager rather than being found twice.
Tool and CRD versions pinned in the CI workflow, each marked with a renovate: comment

packageRules.description: Name the commit after the image. Chart.yaml's appVersion is NOT updated - `^version:` does not match `appVersion:` - so it drifts from image.tag until someone edits it by hand.

Bumping an image is a chart change, so the chart's own version has to move with it. chart-releaser only publishes a chart whose version is new, and ct.yaml sets check-version-increment, so without this every Renovate PR would fail CI and nothing would ever be released.

Patch and minor application updates are the maintenance load this repo exists to avoid. Merge them automatically once CI is green — CI renders every chart, validates against the Kubernetes schemas and resolves every image, so a bad bump fails before it merges.
Major application updates change behaviour and often need a values or migration change. Always review these by hand.
LinuxServer images carry an -lsNNN build suffix that moves independently of the upstream application version, so they need the loose versioning scheme rather than semver.
The Servarr applications use four-part versions (4.0.19.2979) that are not semver.

qBittorrent's official image publishes an lt2 variant built against libtorrent 2.x, which upstream documents as having memory and performance problems. Never propose it as an update to the default build.
Never propose pre-release builds as updates.
Keep the CI toolchain current - action versions and the tool pins in the workflow. These only affect the pipeline, so automerge them.
